questions.stem: All of the following sites have NIS EXCEPT?
questions.solutionHtml:
Placenta

The placenta does not express NIS.



Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology 26th Edition Page no. 105, 107.

questions.stem: Which one of the following substances will have higher concentration in the tubular lumen after passing through PCT?
questions.solutionHtml:
Chloride

Both glucose and amino acids are reabsorbed to a greater extent, and bicarbonate is also significantly reabsorbed in the PCT. Therefore, chloride is more likely to have a higher concentration in the tubular lumen compared to the other substances listed.



Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition Page no. 349.

questions.stem: When to do pulmonary assessments preoperatively in COPD?
questions.solutionHtml:
FEV1/FVC < 0.7; FEV1< 80%
  • This criterion indicates that if the FEV1/FVC ratio is less than 0.7 and the absolute FEV1 value is less than 80% predicted, it suggests airflow limitation consistent with COPD.
  • These parameters are used to classify the severity of COPD based on the Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) guidelines.


Ganong's Review Of Medical physiology, 20th Edit page no: 617, Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 21st Edition Page no: 2159, Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 20th Edition Page no: 1964, 2026.

questions.stem: For a skeletal muscle, latent period: 10msec, contraction period 40msec and relaxation period was 20msec. Calculate tetanizing frequency:
questions.solutionHtml:
25/sec

Tetanizing frequency= 1/contraction period=1/(40 msec) =1/0.04 per sec= 25 per second.



Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition Page no. 105.

questions.stem: All of the following will shift the O2 dissociation curve to the right EXCEPT:
questions.solutionHtml:
Increased HbF

The factor that will NOT shift the O2 dissociation curve to the right is "Increased HbF" since it causes a leftward shift instead.



Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition Page 640, 641, 548, 631, 632.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not an amphipathic lipid?
questions.solutionHtml:
Triglycerides
  • Triglycerides are NOT amphipathic lipids.
  • Triglycerides, also known as triacylglycerols, consist of three fatty acid chains attached to a glycerol backbone.
  • They do not have any significant hydrophilic regions, and their structure is entirely hydrophobic.
  • Triglycerides serve as energy storage molecules and are NOT amphipathic lipids.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition Page no. 9.

questions.stem: Nerve injury with outer axon sheath and nerve fibers intact, inner axon damaged?
questions.solutionHtml:
Axonotmesis

The nerve injury with the outer axon sheath and nerve fibers intact, but the inner axon damaged, is referred to as "Axonotmesis."



Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition Page no 9.

questions.stem: Which of the following is detected by the Pacinian corpuscle?
questions.solutionHtml:
Pressure

The Pacinian corpuscle is a type of mechanoreceptor, and it is primarily responsible for detecting "Pressure."



Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition Page no: 158, 159.Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition Page no:599, 600.

questions.stem: At atmospheric temperature of 47 degree celsius, body loses temperature mainly by:
questions.solutionHtml:
Evaporation

At an atmospheric temperature of 47 degrees Celsius, the body mainly loses temperature by "Evaporation."



Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 41st Edition Page no. 150.

questions.stem: An athlete was exercising in the park. After reaching an equilibrium state, what is the MET score if 1500ml of oxygen consumption per minute for healthy 70kg adult male with basal oxygen consumption is 250 ml/ minute:
questions.solutionHtml:
6
  • The metabolic equivalent of task (MET)is the objective measure of the ratio of the rate at which a person expends energy, relative to the mass of that person, while performing some specific physical activity compared to a reference, set by convention at 3.5 mL of oxygen per kilogram per minute, which is roughly equivalent to the energy expended when sitting quietly.
  • MET score= oxygen consumption during exercise/basal oxygen consumption (taken as one MET)
  • MET score=1500/250=6


Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition Page no 821.
